function: DDPG actor jointly outputs BS beamforming and the phase shifts of two RISs to maximize downlink spectral efficiency at the train mobile relay (p. 6).
system: Downlink MIMO in a tunnel: BS 8 antennas, train relay 8 antennas, two reflecting RISs of 16 elements, 28 GHz mmWave, 350 km/h (p. 4, 11).
method: DDPG with proportional (PBPR) and rank-based (RBPR) prioritized experience replay on TD error; actor-critic with two hidden layers; reinforcement learning trained off-line (p. 7-9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave paths, Gaussian gains with path loss and shadow fading, Doppler, outdated CSI via Jakes' correlation; no standard model or dataset (p. 4-5).
test_conditions: 15000 episodes of 50 steps at 350 km/h, 16 elements per RIS; SE also reported at 50 and 600 km/h and 9-49 elements; retraining unstated (p. 11, 14-15).
baselines: URBR-DDPG (uniform replay DDPG adapted from [14]) only; FP and WMMSE are named in the introduction but not compared (p. 2, 13-14).
metrics: Instantaneous and average spectral efficiency (bps/Hz), actor loss, training stability; SE versus velocity and RIS elements; step and episode duration (p. 11-15).
complexity: Training time complexity per algorithm in O(.) form, inference and memory complexity; measured step, episode and total training time on GPU and CPU (Table I) (p. 10-11).
q1_support: p. 4: "following the Saleh-Valenzuela channel model". Gains are complex Gaussian with path loss and shadow fading (p. 5); a custom simulator, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "observing the effect of changing the velocity of the HST-MR and the number of reflecting elements of the RISs". Sweeps only; no model trained in one setting is said to be tested in another, and transfer learning is future work (p. 15).
q3_support: p. 15: "its advantage over the modified benchmark URBR-DDPG algorithm". The only baseline is the learned URBR-DDPG; FP and WMMSE are only named on p. 2 and no non-learned method is compared in Figs. 15-18.
q4_support: p. 10: "The overall training complexity (time complexity) for the URBR-DDPG algorithm can be formulated as" an O(.) expression; PBPR and RBPR are given likewise, and Table I (p. 11) lists measured step and training times.
q5_support: p. 5: "the time-varying channel gain which follows a complex Gaussian distribution similar to that used in [14]". Data come from the authors' own simulator; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included, area 3: DDPG variants learn the BS beamformer and the phase shifts of two RISs (p. 6). q3=0 because the only baseline is URBR-DDPG, itself a learned method. q4=1 from the complexity analysis (p. 9-10) and measured runtimes (Table I, p. 11). Retraining per velocity or RIS size is not stated, and the RIS-size sweep changes the action dimension, so q2=0. PDF title and DOI match on p. 1.
